name: "Freezer Friendly" Italian Lentil Soup with Kale (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 16 cups of soup or 8 (2-cup) servings.
Wash and dry the fresh produce
instructions.secondary_message:
4 stick celery
1 small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley
1 bunch kale

instructions.primary_message: Peel, trim, and medium dice carrots. Place in a large bowl.
Trim and slice celery crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Add to the bowl with the carrots.
Peel, halve, and small dice onions; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 10 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp Italian seasoning
1 ½ tsp basil, dried
1 ¼ tsp salt
1 tsp rosemary, dried
¾ tsp black pepper
½ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the veggies are softened, add lentils, broth, tomatoes, and bay leaves to the pot; stir to combine the soup, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat (skim away any foam that rises to the surface). Once boiling, uncover, reduce to a simmer, and cook, stirring occasionally and breaking up the tomatoes with a spoon, until lentils are tender and soup has thickened slightly, 25-30 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
10 cups chicken or vegetable broth
1 (28 oz) can canned whole tomatoes

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in the reserved bowl.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the parsley.

When the lentils are done, add parsley and kale to the pot in handfuls, waiting for the greens to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Continue to cook until kale is completely wilted, 2-3 minutes more.
Add vinegar to the pot, stir to combine, and remove from heat. Set aside to cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
Once the soup has cooled, divide between containers.

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 3 months. HEATING: For best results, thaw soup in the fridge overnight. Warm in a saucepan set over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 5 minutes.
CHEF'S NOTE: Top soup with grated Parmesan and more fresh parsley, if desired. Serve with crusty bread on the side and enjoy!
